deviations: fingerprint.lua has 20 checks, not the 19 in design.md §5. The count is 18, plus 1 because the flip loop grows with the ninth token, plus 1 for the new agreement check. compat's run of today's file on a nine-token word already counted 19 (16 passed + 3 failed) for the same reason. Any doc or evidence that says 19 should say 20 [M].

The bit-token agreement check asks both the parser fold (`1 << 32`, what a dump's constants hold) and a runtime operand (`a << 32` with a vararg, what a restored thread runs). design.md says 'at run time' only. The two must agree with each other and with the token; a mixed result matches neither token. The chunk is compiled with load(), so a parser without the operators fails only this check.

bitop.lua is re-derived under B and has 7 checks, not 6. (1) The probe's `x << 13` on a 53-bit x raises under B, so x is masked to 40 bits before the shift. (2) h XORs `i << 40` instead of `1 << 40`, so its final value has 53 bits rather than under 32. (3) Check 1 compares with PUC 5.3.6's values instead of only 'finishes'. (4) The folded-constants check now uses exact constants (1<<62, ~0>>11, ~(2^53-1), -2^63|0), since `1 << 62 | 1` and `~0 >> 1` raise under B. (5) New check 7: those inexact expressions raise B's message in the restored coroutine. (6) It ends with `return fail` (the harness convention) instead of os.exit. As a result today's build fails 3 checks, not the 1 in design.md §6 [M].

The negctl bitword arm also asserts that the sabotaged binary's banner word ends in '.bit32', so a toggle that did not take shows up as such. Not in the design; same style as the other arms. The grep has no '$' because a Windows binary writes CRLF.
